title: Ops Conductor: Telemetry Gateway for incident automation and evidence bundling
creator: Priya Patel
description:
Problem: On-call engineers spend significant time collecting scattered traces, logs, and metric slices when responding to incidents. Existing integrations send raw links and full traces which overwhelm PD/Slack context cards and slow triage.

Goal: Build an Ops Conductor Telemetry Gateway (OTG) — a lightweight service that listens to observability signals (traces, metrics anomalies, log spikes), condenses evidence into a compact 'incident bundle', scores and ranks signals, and pushes structured attachments to PagerDuty and Slack as part of an automated incident creation/append flow. The focus is production-grade reliability, privacy-preserving evidence snippets, and low-latency attachment generation.

Scope:
- Ingest events from tracing-hook stream, metric alerts, and log-alert pipeline.
- Normalise signal payloads, compute a relevance score, and select top N snippets.
- Generate PD and Slack attachments with: short summary, high-salience spans, metric sparkline, top log snippets, and links to full artifacts.
- Provide API for runbook template selection and inline checklist insertion at incident creation time.
- Feature flags for per-team rollout, throttle controls, and fallbacks to link-only mode.

Non-goals:
- Full postmortem generation (this ticket produces a skeleton and evidence bundle; PM will own postmortem auto-fill in follow-up).
- Replacing existing long-term storage or dashboards.

Success metrics: reduction in mean time to acknowledge (MTTA) for P0/P1 incidents by 15% in pilot teams, and >90% of PD attachments under 100KB.
technical_notes:
Architecture: deploy OTG as a small horizontally-scalable service in telemetry cluster. Input streams: 1) traces via trace-hook UDP/gRPC forwarder (sampled prefix fetch API), 2) metrics via alert-bridge (prom-alerts + anomaly events), 3) log spikes via alerts pipeline. Normaliser module converts to canonical event shape, then scorer computes a numeric relevance score using heuristics (error rate deltas, latency regression magnitude, span-error density). Evidence selector uses a sliding-window KV-backed cache to fetch prefetched span prefixes and top logs for the time window. Attachments are rendered as structured JSON cards with short text + condensed snippets; PD integration uses Events API v2 with dedup keys; Slack integration uses blocks with collapsed code snippets and 'Open in Console' deep links.

Operational constraints: must respect PII filters from log-redaction service, enforce per-tenant rate limits, and backpressure to avoid incident creation storms. Implement circuit-breaker and degrade to link-only mode when attachment generation latency > 250ms.

Implementation plan: 1) service skeleton + input adapters (2 sprints), 2) canonicalizer + scoring (1 sprint), 3) PD/Slack rendering + feature flags (1 sprint), 4) e2e pilot with two platform teams and add telemetry dashboards (1 sprint).

Key libraries/infra: gRPC + Kafka consumer, internal redaction lib, console deep-link helper, feature-flag sdk, Sentry + datadog for OTG metrics.

Backward compatibility: PD events will include a fallback 'attachments' field that older runbooks ignore. Provide toggle to disable auto-attach and only include link references.
acceptance_criteria: OTG ingests trace/metric/log events and produces a normalized event within 100ms end-to-end for sampled events
PagerDuty incidents created by OTG include a structured attachment no larger than 100KB in 90% of cases
Slack channel posts created by OTG render a compact summary + a maximum of 3 condensed code/log snippets
Feature flag allows disabling attachments per-team and falls back to link-only without errors
Automated test harness validates PII redaction and enforces redaction rules
Pilot with two teams shows at least 10% reduction in MTTA for qualifying incidents

High-volume incidents might cause PD/Slack API rate limits to trigger; need batching/debounce
Scoring heuristics may prioritise irrelevant signals initially; requires tuning and telemetry
OTG becomes a single point of failure for incident context if fallback not robust
